:::{#exm-symmetric-bilinear-form}
#### A symmetric bilinear form

<!-- no-figure: the example computes two numbers from one small matrix -->

Let

$$
\matr{S} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \vx = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}, \quad \vy = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

The [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) $\matr{S}$ is [symmetric](#def-symmetric-matrix),
because its two [off-diagonal entries](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-off-diagonal-entry) are both $2$,
so its [bilinear form](#def-bilinear-form) is a [symmetric bilinear form](#def-symmetric-bilinear-form).
At $\vx$ and $\vy$, that form is

$$
\ba
\bformf{\matr{S}}{\vx}{\vy}
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -1 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-bilinear-form)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd 3 + 2 \cd (-1) \\ 2 \cd 3 + 1 \cd (-1) \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply the matrix by } \vy \text{)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\\
&= 1 \cd 1 + 2 \cd 5
&& \text{(multiply the row by the column)}
\\
&= 11.
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

With the vectors swapped, it is

$$
\ba
\bformf{\matr{S}}{\vy}{\vx}
&= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(@def-bilinear-form)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd 1 + 2 \cd 2 \\ 2 \cd 1 + 1 \cd 2 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply the matrix by } \vx \text{)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 \end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\\
&= 3 \cd 5 + (-1) \cd 4
&& \text{(multiply the row by the column)}
\\
&= 11,
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

the same value, as @thm-symmetric-bilinear-form-swap says it must be.
By contrast, $\matr{A}$ in @exm-bilinear-form is not symmetric,
so its bilinear form is not a symmetric bilinear form,
and swapping the vectors changed its value from $-5$ to $9$.

:::
